 Scottie Barnes got himself 17 points (7-of-15 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, six assists, three steals, a three, and five turnovers in loss to Nuggets. 
 Scottie filled up the box score despite not having the greatest night scoring the ball. The Raptors as a whole didn’t do a great job defensively in this game which resulted in their blowout. Scottie has had so many good performances recently that there’s no need to panic. The next opportunity to bounce back will be against the Bucks on Friday. 
 Scottie Barnes 
 TOR 
 Forward-Guard 
 #4 
 Scottie Barnes accumulated 22 points (7-of-15 FGs, 8-of-15 FTs), 15 rebounds, eight assists and two steals in Monday’s win over the Clippers. 
 Barnes appeared to aggravate his sore left hip during the third quarter, but he returned to the game after some time on the bench. And it’s a good thing he did, as the Raptors forward was outstanding in the fourth quarter. Barnes recorded 15 points, eight rebounds, one assist and two steals in the quarter, helping the Raptors erase a 13-point deficit to win by seven. Barnes struggled at the foul line, but that was his only negative on his final stat line.

 Forward-Guard 
 #4 
 Scottie Barnes (hip) is available for Monday’s game against the Clippers while Jakob Poeltl (shoulder) is out. 
 While Barnes is good to go after initially being questionable, Poeltl will miss a second straight game. Trayce Jackson-Davis started Sunday’s loss to the Lakers but wasn’t productive enough to merit streaming in any fantasy league.

 Scottie Barnes (hip) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Clippers. 
 Barnes popped up on the injury report Monday afternoon as questionable with left hip tightness. While the injury doesn’t sound overly serious, Barnes could be on the wrong side of questionable here. If he’s ruled out, Collin Murray-Boyles could move into the starting lineup. 
 Scottie Barnes 
 TOR 
 Forward-Guard 
 #4 
 Scottie Barnes finished Sunday’s loss to the Lakers with 29 points (11-of-20 FGs, 7-of-13 FTs), six rebounds, five assists and two steals. 
 Barnes’ mid-range mastery helped him score 29 points, and he’s scored at least 28 in three straight and four of his last five games. The exception was the October 25 loss to the Timberwolves, in which the Raptors’ star went scoreless. With Kawhi Leonard (knee) out for a few weeks, Barnes will need to shoulder more responsibility on both ends of the floor. And he’s shown the ability to do that in the past.

 Scottie Barnes with a career high 41 points (19-of-34 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, two steals, and a three in the 121-114 loss to the Magic. 
 Scottie Barnes was carrying the offense in the first half for the Raptors with 23 first half points. No one else on the team which helped Scottie’s value, but it didn’t exactly help the Raptors as the Magic got revenge on this one. Scottie has been an absolute monster this season will continue to put up crazy performances with and without Kawhi Leonard playing. 
 Scottie Barnes

 Forward-Guard 
 #4 
 Scottie Barnes has 28 points (11-of-17 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, four assists, three steals, and two blocks in 129-99 win against the Magic. 
 With no Kawhi Leonard, Scottie Barnes made up the difference and kept the defense aggressive in this game. He’s very good as a roamer and can get a lot of his defensive numbers that way. If you drafted Scottie Barnes, you should be feeling very happy about that decision and should be in contention to finish in the top 10 of fantasy rankings this season. 
 Ja'Kobe Walter 
 TOR 
 Guard 
 #14 
 The Toronto Raptors will start Immanuel Quickley, Ja’Kobe Walter, RJ Barrett, Scottie Barnes, and Jakob Poeltl against the Magic on Friday. 
 Kawhi Leonard is out with knee soreness, so Ja’Kobe Walter will get the start against the Magic. He’s useful if you need some points and 3’s but he likely will not be much more than a deeper league guy. Look for Barnes, Quickley, and Barrett to pick up the slack without Kawhi. 
 Scottie Barnes 
 TOR 
 Forward-Guard 
 #4 
 Scottie Barnes failed to score in Sunday’s loss to the Timberwolves, finishing with three rebounds, three assists, four steals and one blocked shot. 
 With Kawhi Leonard (knee) unavailable, the Timberwolves could focus more of their defensive attention on Barnes. Unfortunately for the Raptors and fantasy managers who are rostering him, Barnes couldn’t buy a basket. He shot 0-of-12 from the field and did not attempt a free throw. Given Barnes’ track record, managers should expect to see him bounce back from Sunday’s performance. But it was a rough way to end Week 1. 
 Scottie Barnes

 Scottie Barnes scored 28 points (12-of- FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), fourteen rebounds, five assists, two steals, two blocks and a three on Friday. 
 You would like Scottie to hit some more 3’s and not turn the ball over 8 times, but that’s not why you have him. These are the stat lines that you wanted when you drafted Scottie as early as you did. There are not many players that can get 28 points, 14 rebounds, and 5 assists in fantasy. Sit back and enjoy the high-level production.

 Victor Wembanyama finished Wednesday’s win over the Mavericks with 52 points (16-of-28 FGs, 19-of-23 FTs), 24 rebounds, two assists, two steals, eight blocks and one three-pointer.
 The Mavericks aren’t the first team to have no answer for Wembanyama, and they certainly won’t be the last. He was dominant throughout, becoming the second player in league history to finish a game with at least 50 points, 20 rebounds and five blocks since the NBA began recording blocks as an official stat. The other player: Bob McAdoo in 1974. Wembanyama’s 52 points are a new career high, and he shot 1-of-8 from beyond the arc. Just an incredible showing from one of the NBA’s elite talents. Wembanyama appeared to tweak his right ankle in the fourth quarter, but he did not receive medical attention while on the bench and returned for crunch time.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Devin Booker had 33 points (9-of-19 FGs, 13-of-13 FTs), one rebound, two assists and two three-pointers against the Trail Blazers on Wednesday. 
 Booker was just 2-of-8 from behind the three-point line in this one, but made his hay at the foul line as he drained all 13 of his free throw attempts on his way to a 33-point game. The 30-year-old guard played almost 34 minutes despite fouling out for the second consecutive game. Booker and the Suns will be back on the floor Thursday at home against the Magic.

 Reed Sheppard finished Wednesday’s loss to the Timberwolves with 14 points (5-of-12 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), two rebounds, two assists, three steals and three three-pointers.
 Sheppard has now scored in double figures in three of the six games he’s played this season. Against the Timberwolves, his final stat line included a season-high three steals. With the Rockets signing Marcus Smart (four points, one rebound, one assist, one block and one three-pointer) during the offseason and Fred VanVleet back from a torn ACL, Sheppard’s upside in redraft leagues is limited as long as both veterans are healthy.

 Fred VanVleet amassed 18 points (6-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, three assists and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
 Back in the Rockets’ lineup after sitting out Monday’s win over the Celtics, VanVleet played 30 minutes against the Timberwolves. Even though he shot 50 percent from the field on Wednesday, the Rockets’ guard is making just 39 percent of his attempts this season. VanVleet has long offered little value in that category. But most fantasy managers know he’ll do enough across the board to be a solid category-league option.

 RJ Barrett put up 22 points (7-of-17 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, and three 3-pointers in 128-109 loss to the Nuggets.
 Barrett led the team in shot attempts in this game and he did a good job scoring the ball. On the season, he’s averaging 20.9 points, 6 rebounds, 3.9 assists, 0.5 steals, and 0.5 blocks, shooting 48.1% from the field, 59.5% from the free throw line, and 31.8% from three. Outside of the free throw percentage, he’s been great for where he was selected in redraft leagues. There’s even room for him to get better once he starts hitting more of his free throws.
